citations.description: assert opens `(` at line 224; no closing `)` before `def _optionality_loop_step_run` at line 229 — unclosed parenthesis is a SyntaxError

findings.criterion: A checked-in test asserts `tests/unit/test_core_optionality.py` and `tests/unit/test_optional.py` collect 9 items under `-m "not integration and not external"`.
findings.detail: The function `test_optionality_suite_still_runs_in_the_default_selection` (lines 212–228) has a syntax error: the `assert` at line 224 opens a parenthesized message `(` that is never closed with `)`. The string literal at line 228 ends and then a new `def` begins at line 229 at module level, inside the unclosed parenthesis. Python raises `SyntaxError` when importing this module, so the guard test does not exist in a runnable form.
findings.remediation: Add the missing closing `)` at the end of line 228 (after the final string literal) to close the assert's message tuple, making the function syntactically valid.

citations.description: Same SyntaxError prevents the test from executing in any scenario

findings.criterion: That test FAILS if a marker excluding either file from the default selection is added.
findings.detail: Because the test module has a SyntaxError (unclosed parenthesis in `test_optionality_suite_still_runs_in_the_default_selection`), the guard cannot run at all — it cannot fail on a bad marker, so the durability property is not demonstrated.

citations.description: Unclosed `(` in assert at line 224 — module-level SyntaxError prevents pytest collection

findings.detail: The SyntaxError in `test_ci_workflow_parity.py` (unclosed parenthesis at line 224–228) causes pytest to report a collection error for the entire module, so the run exits non-zero rather than passing.
